subject: Immediate: EU region service degradation — customer routing steps & post-incident actions
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-11-16T09:12:00Z
Subject: EU region: degraded connectivity detected — initial mitigation

Team,

We observed a network degradation in our primary EU region (eu-west-2) beginning ~09:00Z. Symptoms: elevated 5xx error rates on model endpoints, increased tail latency for streaming responses, and intermittent TLS handshake failures for a subset of customer IP ranges. Cloud provider reports an L3 networking fabric instability affecting a handful of AZs — they've opened a ticket but we should assume 1-3 hours for mitigation based on past escalations.

Immediate asks:
- Notify affected customers with clear routing guidance (see suggested copy below).
- Provide short-term routing options: region header override, alternate API endpoint, and DNS-based fallback with low TTL.
- Recommend temporary throttling to reduce error amplification (suggest 10-20% lower QPS where tolerable).

Attachments: eu-failover-playbook.pdf (step-by-step routing), traffic-shift-checklist.csv (canary checklist).

Suggested external message (editable):
- Brief: "We're seeing degraded performance in our EU region. As a precaution, you can route traffic to our US region (us-west-1) or APAC region (ap-southeast-1) by setting X-Redwood-Region or switching endpoints. See our attached failover playbook for step-by-step instructions and monitoring checks."

I'll start preparing the detailed steps and a customer-facing playbook.

Thanks,
Marcus
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
From: Ops Team <ops@alderbank.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-11-16T09:28:00Z
Subject: Re: EU region: degraded connectivity detected — initial mitigation

Thanks for the heads up. We're seeing a spike in errors on our end as well. Two quick questions: 1) How long do you expect this to last? 2) If we switch to US region, will any data residency settings (logs/audit) be affected? We need rollback instructions if the shift impacts compliance.

— Ops Team (AlderBank)
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Ops Team <ops@alderbank.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-11-16T09:42:00Z
Subject: Re: EU region: degraded connectivity detected — initial mitigation

Hi AlderBank ops —

Short answers up front: 1) ETA unknown; current estimate from provider is 1–3 hours but we'll monitor and update. 2) Data residency: temporary traffic redirection to another region will route inference requests outside eu-west-2; we will not move persisted customer data (logs/audit snapshots) unless explicitly agreed. If you have strict residency constraints, please let us know and we can explore targeted retries or a limited canary.

Actionable routing options (pick one, ordered by operational impact):

A) Header override (recommended for fastest cutover)
- Add header: X-Redwood-Region: us-west-1
- Behavior: request will be serviced by US cluster; no change to API key or token.
- Tradeoffs: higher network latency; audit logs will be tagged with us-west-1.

B) Alternate endpoint (DNS switch)
- Use api-us.redwood-inference.com or api-apac.redwood-inference.com
- Set DNS TTL=60s for quick rollback.
- We recommend a 10% canary for 30 minutes: shift 10% traffic -> monitor 5xx rate and latency -> increase in 10% increments.

C) Model-level fallback (conservative)
- If you rely on specific large variants, consider switching to the compatible smaller variant (gpt-small-v1) for short periods to reduce compute timeouts.

Monitoring checklist (short):
- Watch 5xx rate, stream disconnects, and token-level tail latency.
- Query: region:error_count and region:latency_p95 in the dashboard.
- Set alert: if canary 5xx > 1% for 10 minutes rollback to prior config.

Rollback guidance: revert header or DNS change; if using canary do the inverse (reduce canary to 0%), confirm parsing of logs for any partial requests.

I'll attach a concise 1-page runbook (eu-failover-playbook.pdf) and a CSV checklist with monitoring thresholds (traffic-shift-checklist.csv). Marcus: please confirm we have an automated tracer that annotates requests with original-region so we can reconcile billed tokens and audit retention later. Lauren: can you acknowledge customer-facing messaging edits?

Mina
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Ops Team <ops@alderbank.com>
Date: 2028-11-16T10:05:00Z
Subject: Re: EU region: degraded connectivity detected — initial mitigation

On Wed, Nov 16, 2028 at 09:42 Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com> wrote:
> Mina: please confirm we have an automated tracer that annotates requests with original-region so we can reconcile billed tokens and audit retention later.

Confirmed: requests sent with header override are annotated with original_region and served_region metadata; audit logs will contain both fields. We'll preserve logs in eu-retention for 30 days as usual; however, any ephemeral routing during this incident means inference execution ocurrs outside EU for that request. Finance: billable tokens will reflect the serving region.

Internal follow-up (post-incident action items):
- INF-9821 (Marcus): implement a soft auto-failover that will trigger if eu 5xx rate > 0.5% for 5m (owner: Marcus, ETA: 2028-12-20).
- CS-421 (Lauren): customer comms template + compliance addendum for temporary cross-region routing (owner: Lauren, ETA: 2028-11-20).
- PM-307 (Hannah): evaluate a per-account residency guardrail that prevents automatic cross-region serving for accounts with strict residency (owner: Hannah, ETA: 2029-01-15).

AlderBank: we recommend starting with header override canary at 10% for 30 minutes. I'll join your engineers on a quick call if you want live support.

Marcus
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>

AlderBank ops —

Thanks for bearing with us. The provider reports partial remediation at ~15:30Z; eu error rates are trending back down but we keep the playbook available if you want to perform a controlled shift for safety.

Summary / What we did:
- Notified customers and shared the playbook + checklist.
- Confirmed header override and alternate endpoint options.
- Logged action items for a postmortem and product changes (see INF-9821, CS-421, PM-307).

If you switched any traffic, please reply with the time window and percent of traffic so we can reconcile logs and billing. We'll schedule a 30-minute post-incident review early next week; propose Tue 2028-11-21 15:00Z. If that doesn't work, share a preferred time.

Again — apologies for the disruption. We're treating resilience improvements as a priority and will share the full postmortem once complete.

Best,
Mina Haddad

Redwood Inference
